newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber closes firm on Korea support.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber closes firm on Korea support.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher, recouping midday falls, after late news of Korean support for the SMR 20, traders said.
Tyre-grade RSS3 was also keenly inquired by Bridgestone, said one trader. Other grades were largely ignored.
"We sold about 100 tonnes of the (SMR)20 to Korea at 285 cents ($1.15) a kg," said a trader. "We heard they bought more from others."
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted April RSS1 buyer half cent up at 299 cents a kg. April SMR20 buyer was quoted unchanged at 285.
Traders offered the SMR20 at 286 cents a kg, SMR CV at 352, SMR L at 332, SMR 5 at 295, SMR 10 at 287 and drum latex FOB at 237.
The INRO five-day indicator was down to 229.19 Malaysian/Singaporean cents per kg on March 25, from 229.50 a day earlier. The daily indicator fell to 228.88 from 229.73.
